summary.intent: Drive the Caliper repo's backlog to completion by delegating to worker agents: ship trail 165 (clippy and docs lint hardening) as PRs, then continue with the remaining trails (166 watch perf, 153 three-tools report, 157 agent eval weekly) until done.
summary.outcome: Trail 165 was pushed and linked as seven signed draft PRs (#306-#312) with bodies. Earlier PRs #300-#305 had merged, and three workers (trails 166, 153, 157) were started; the crate-wide missing_docs deny, the ADR 0006/0007 note, and several merges and decisions remain pending.

repo: Clippy in CI (justfile x2, .moon/tasks.yml) previously ran without --all-targets and excluded caliper-docgen-napi; it now uses `--workspace --all-targets` on branch ci/lint-all-targets, which surfaced 29 test-code lint errors.
clippy::exit is enforced as a workspace lint, replacing a unit test that grepped source for process::exit. Reasoned allows live at the watch keyboard quit and the fake-tsc helper.
Core has #![deny(missing_debug_implementations)]; WatchSession needed a manual Debug impl and IncrementalUpdate derives Debug.
NAPI copies `///` doc comments into generated typings, so packages/napi/binding.d.ts must be hand-synced when binding docs change (napi build was not run).

ExtractionStats fields components_skipped, tier1_count, tier3_count and opaque_count are never set by the pipeline and are always 0; dts_files_parsed counts cache lookups (hits plus misses), not parsed files.
Doc comments on clap args change `--help` output (e.g. `caliper-docgen completions --help` now describes SHELL).
A crate-wide #![deny(missing_docs)] in core only compiles once the four types/ docs branches and docs/core-api-rest (about 18 public items outside types/) are merged.

Merge dependencies: #306 before #307 (stacked), #300 before #301; #308 edits types/semantic.rs, which #301 may also touch, so merge main into whichever lands second. Trails 153 and 157 both edit weekly.py.
Release flow: the first attested release has not run yet, so the backfill path is unproven; three release runs were queued behind CI backlog.
workflow: zsh does not word-split unquoted variables, so a `for b in $list` loop treated seven branch names as one; use arrays or an explicit list in push/link scripts.

Perf-measurement workers should run while the machine is quiet; other CPU-heavy workers were held back or told to keep local runs few so timings are not disturbed, and the perf worker reports load average and spread.
GitHub PR body edits can hit transient TLS timeouts; verify bodies after editing and retry failures.
Worker agents were run in isolated worktrees and told not to push, open PRs or merge; the parent verifies signatures, then pushes and links them.
Workers were told to recommend dropping any perf branch whose gain is under 1 ms or inside noise, since an earlier estimate shrank when measured.

friction: The first push/link script failed because of the zsh word-splitting quirk, costing one retry.
PR body edits for #308 and #309 failed on a transient GitHub TLS timeout and needed a retry.
CI backlog left release runs queued and PR checks unread, so release behavior could not yet be validated.
Seven new PRs plus other open ones (#291, #299-#302, #304-#312 at the time of the summary) create a heavy review load for the user.
open_items: Create lint/deny-missing-docs-crate-wide (one-line crate-wide deny) after #308, #309, #310 and #312 merge.
Push and open PRs for trail 166 (watch perf), trail 153 (oracle/three-tools-report) and trail 157 (feat/agent-eval-weekly) when the workers report; drop perf branches that are not worth shipping.
Write a short ADR 0006/0007 follow-up noting that a session re-asks the checker after a dependency edit (behavior from #300).

User decisions pending: merge #306-#312 and release PR #291, watch the first release run, whether to write an ADR for feat/cross-file-render-evidence (trail 156, recovers one antd component, recommended skip), whether to scope a follow-up for the ~70 ms / 175 MiB shadcn dependency-loading cost (trail 154), and whether to pin macos-26 in the release matrix.
Deferred with no trail yet: Rust 2024 edition, the indexing_slicing and wildcard_enum_match_arm lints, and a breaking-API bundle for the next minor bump.
Merge main into the second of the branches that edit weekly.py (trails 153 and 157).
